title: std::string Basics
learningObjectives: Create, assign and append std::string values.
Use size, empty and character access appropriately.
Choose std::string instead of manually managed text buffers.

understand.concept: std::string manages text and its length, and supports assignment, comparison, concatenation and member operations.
understand.whyItMatters: It is a safer, easier default for ordinary text than manually managed character buffers.
understand.explain: Use size, clear and normal string operations; avoid manual terminator management.

examples.title: Initialize string
examples.explanation: string tracks length without manual termination.

examples.title: Assign and clear
examples.explanation: Assignment replaces content and clear empties it.

examples.title: Change a character
examples.explanation: Indexing modifies a character within bounds.

practise.guidedTask: For std::string Basics, trace each example and record the collection type, size/capacity where relevant, valid index range, values before and after each operation, and what the code prints. Identify the key boundary case.
practise.independentTask: Write a C++ mini-task focused on std::string Basics: use a small collection of values/text, perform at least three meaningful operations, and test normal, empty or boundary, and invalid-index/input cases. Explain your collection choice and expected output.
hints: Select the collection type and justify its size behavior.
Trace initialization and current element values.
Use bounds-aware access for potentially invalid indexes.
Prefer direct traversal when the index is not required.
Test empty, first, last and out-of-range scenarios.
